references.text: Laying hands on the head of the sacrificial animal is an important part of the burnt offering ceremony, where the one making the sacrifice identifies with the offering.
For the sin offering, the priest shall lay his hand on the bull's head before the Lord, the same ritual as at the consecration of Aaron and his sons.
This verse describes the actual execution of what is commanded in Exodus 29:10, where Moses brings forward the sin offering bull and Aaron and his sons lay their hands on its head.
On the Day of Atonement, Aaron lays both hands on the goat's head and confesses the people's sins, showing the significance of laying on of hands for the transfer of sin.
The Levites lay their hands on the bulls' heads during their consecration, the same ritual action as at the priests' consecration.
The entrance area of the tabernacle was the place where offerings were to be brought forward, as described in the consecration ritual.
The book of Hebrews refers to the Old Testament sacrifices with bulls and goats as a shadow of Christ's perfect offering.
